hints: Complete the square to express $f(x)$ as $\frac{15}{2} - 2(x - \frac{3}{2})^2$.
State the range $f(x) \le \frac{15}{2}$ using the maximum value.
walkthrough:
Identify constants $a = \frac{15}{2}, b = 2, c = \frac{3}{2}$ and determine the maximum value:
$$\text{Since } 2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}, \text{ the maximum value is } \frac{15}{2}$$

hints: The turning point of $f(x)$ is a maximum at $(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{15}{2})$.
Reflect in the $x$-axis so the maximum becomes a minimum at $(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{15}{2})$.
Translate the minimum from $(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{15}{2})$ to $(0, 0)$ using vector $\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{3}{2}\\\frac{15}{2}\end{pmatrix}$.
walkthrough:
Identify the turning point of the original downward parabola:
$$\text{Maximum vertex at } \left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{15}{2}\right)$$

Reflect the curve in the $x$-axis to turn the maximum into a minimum:
$$\text{Reflection in the } x\text{-axis (giving vertex at } \left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{15}{2}\right)\text{)}$$

Translate the reflected vertex to the origin $(0, 0)$:
$$\text{Translation by vector } \begin{pmatrix} -\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{15}{2} \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: Since the vertex of $3+6x-2x^2$ is at $x = 1.5$, the restricted domain $x \le 0$ lies entirely to the left of the vertex.
On $x \le 0$, the function is strictly increasing and monotonic.
Explain that each $y$-value corresponds to exactly one $x$-value (it passes the horizontal line test).
walkthrough:
Analyze the restricted branch $g(x) = 3 + 6x - 2x^2$ for $x \le 0$:
$$\text{The vertex of the parabola is at } x = \frac{3}{2} > 0$$
$$\text{For } x \le 0, \text{ the graph is strictly increasing and monotonic (contained in the second and third quadrants)}$$

Explain why $g$ is a one-to-one function:
$$g \text{ is one-to-one because each } y\text{-value is associated with a single unique } x\text{-value (it passes the horizontal line test)}$$

hints: Take the square root, choosing the negative branch since the original domain is $x \le 0$.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the completed-square formula $y = \frac{15}{2} - 2(x - \frac{3}{2})^2$ to make $x$ the subject:
$$2\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{15}{2} - y \implies \left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{15}{4} - \frac{1}{2}y$$

Take the square root, selecting the negative branch because the domain is $x \le 0 < \frac{3}{2}$:
$$x - \frac{3}{2} = -\sqrt{\frac{15}{4} - \frac{1}{2}y} \implies x = \frac{3}{2} - \sqrt{\frac{15}{4} - \frac{1}{2}y}$$

Swap variables to state the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$:
$$g^{-1}(x) = \frac{3}{2} - \sqrt{\frac{15}{4} - \frac{1}{2}x}$$
